parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/order-controller.ts is an Express HTTP adapter. Every job it does is transport work, which belongs in an infrastructure layer. It sets up routes (routes()), reads and checks request parameters (idFrom, stateFrom), maps each route to a target state and passes it on (transition), and turns errors into HTTP status codes (handle). The real work is handed to application services: CatalogueService.addProduct/listProducts and OrderService.placeOrder/listOrders/getOrder/advanceOrder/cancelOrder. Whether a state transition is allowed is decided in OrderService.advanceOrder, not here. stateFrom checks the query string against the domain's own orderStates list. That is input parsing and does not copy any domain rule. Throwing DomainError for bad input is a minor oddity in naming, not a business rule in the wrong layer. No persistence or domain logic is embedded.
